The numbers 1, 2, ..., 2100 are written on a board. Every second, Mark takes two numbers on the board, \( a \) and \( b \), erases them, and replaces them with \( \gcd(a, b) \) and \( \operatorname{lcm}(a, b) \). Mark stops once any move he makes will not change the numbers written on the board. Compute the number of divisors of the 2026th smallest positive integer written on the board when he finishes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let \(v_p(n)\) denote the exponent of prime \(p\) in \(n\).

In one move, replacing \(a,b\) by \(\gcd(a,b),\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)\) changes the pair of \(p\)-exponents \((v_p(a),v_p(b))\) into
\[
(\min(v_p(a),v_p(b)),\max(v_p(a),v_p(b))).
\]
Thus, for every prime \(p\), the multiset of \(p\)-exponents on the board is invariant.

When Mark stops, every move changes nothing, so every pair of board numbers is comparable by divisibility. Hence the final numbers form a divisibility chain. Sort them as
\[
x_1 \le x_2 \le \cdots \le x_{2100}.
\]
Then \(x_i \mid x_j\) whenever \(i<j\), so for each prime \(p\), the sequence
\[
v_p(x_1),v_p(x_2),\dots,v_p(x_{2100})
\]
is nondecreasing. Since the multiset of these exponents is invariant, it must be the sorted list of the exponents of \(p\) among the numbers \(1,2,\dots,2100\).

We need \(x_{2026}\). There are
\[
2100-2026+1=75
\]
entries from \(x_{2026}\) to the end. For a prime \(p\) and integer \(k\ge 1\), the final entries divisible by \(p^k\) are exactly the last
\[
\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^k} \right\rfloor
\]
entries. Therefore \(x_{2026}\) is divisible by \(p^k\) iff
\[
\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^k} \right\rfloor \ge 75.
\]
Since \(2100/75=28\), this is equivalent to
\[
p^k \le 28.
\]

Now compute the relevant exponents:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
p & \max\{k: p^k\le 28\} \\ \hline
2 & 4 \\
3 & 3 \\
5 & 2 \\
7,11,13,17,19,23 & 1
\end{array}
\]

So
\[
x_{2026}=2^4\cdot 3^3\cdot 5^2\cdot 7\cdot 11\cdot 13\cdot 17\cdot 19\cdot 23.
\]

Its number of positive divisors is
\[
(4+1)(3+1)(2+1)(1+1)^6
=5\cdot 4\cdot 3\cdot 2^6
=3840.
\]

\[
\boxed{3840}
\]
